title: Hoshin Kanri
subtitle: Connect your company vision to daily team action without losing
useWhen: anything in translation Your company has a clear vision and your team works hard but there is a gap between the strategic direction and what people are actually working on day to day. The vision stays at the top and doesn't reach the ground.
howToUse: Hoshin Kanri (Japanese: direction management) is a strategic planning and execution framework developed in Japan in the 1950s, refined at Toyota and Bridgestone, and adopted by many Fortune 500 companies. It cascades organisational objectives through every level of the company using a 'catchball' process goals are thrown back and forth between leadership and teams until both sides agree on what is achievable and how it connects. The result is a company where every person's daily work is visibly connected to the company's annual and long-term goals.
steps: Start with your True North, your 3–5 year vision before setting annual objectives.
Use the catchball process: share objectives with teams, ask them to set their own targets, adjust together.
Limit to 3–5 annual breakthrough objectives, Hoshin Kanri is about focus, not comprehensiveness.

Review monthly: are the team-level actions actually moving the company-level metrics? Catchball only works if leadership actually adjusts the target when a team pushes back, if it's just a one-way announcement dressed up as dialogue, the process is theater, and your team will spot it fast.
origin: Yoji Akao, Toyota / Bridgestone — Hoshin Kanri, Japan, 1950s–1960s
promptBody:
Act as a Hoshin Kanri strategy consultant.
Company vision (3–5 years)  :  [WHERE YOU ARE HEADING]
This year's priority                 :  [THE ONE BREAKTHROUGH OBJECTIVE FOR THIS YEAR]
Team structure                       :   [LIST YOUR TEAMS OR FUNCTIONAL AREAS]
Build a Hoshin Kanri cascade:
TRUE NORTH               :  The 3–5 year vision in one clear sentence
ANNUAL OBJECTIVE  :  The single most important thing to achieve this year
TEAM OBJECTIVES     :  For each team what they must deliver to support the annual  
                                            objective
MONTHLY MILESTONES  : Key proof points for each quarter
CATCHBALL QUESTIONS : 3 questions I should ask each team lead to align their objectives
WARNING SIGNALS           :  What would tell me the cascade has broken down?
Hoshin Kanri Hierarchy
Company Vision & Goals
Overall vision and annual objectives of
the company
Department Goals
Objectives set by each department
Team Daily Actions
Speciﬁc tasks performed by teams daily
proTip:
The most common Hoshin failure is confusing activity alignment with outcome
alignment. Every team can be busy doing things that connect to the objective on paper
but don't move the metric. Build the cascade around outcomes at every level  not
initiatives. If you can't draw a straight line from a team member's daily work to a
company metric, the cascade has a gap.
